partial_result_check: Computer-verified in a fresh script: trefoil (xyx=yxy) surjects onto A5 but not A6 or A7. Figure-eight (w=x^-1yxy^-1) surjects onto A4 and A6 but not A5, A7 or A8, and has no S3 quotient, as det=5 requires. n>=9 not rerun (would take more than 30s). The trefoil argument (centre maps trivially, factor through C2*C3, Miller's (2,3)-generation) is correct.
notes: Found no resolution of Dunfield-Thurston Q7.6 or of the infinitely-many-n version, for knots or for hyperbolic 3-manifolds. Sawin-Wood (2022) handle random 3-manifolds, not fixed groups. Baader-Kjuchukova cover S_n quotients with transposition meridians only, which gives A_n quotients of the commutator subgroup, not of G_K. Long-Reid give PSL2(p) quotients, not A_n. Minor: W omits n=5 for the trefoil.

partial_result_check: The PPP-hardness reduction is correct. Take n=m+2. Pad 2^m real pigeons with 2^m+1 dummies, mapped injectively to the 2^m+1 dummy holes. Send the pigeon with C(x)=0 to dummy hole #1, so a collision with dummy #1 decodes to a zero-solution. Embed holes as h -> (h, parity h), which gives even weight. No two even-weight strings are adjacent, so every solution is a collision that decodes to a PIGEON solution.
notes: Found no TFNP or complexity treatment of Huang's theorem. Jain-Li-Robere-Xun (Ramsey/t-PPP) and Laplante et al. (TOCT 2026, linear-dependence proof) do not address it. The crux is the sqrt(n) threshold: degree >=1 follows from pigeonhole on a coordinate matching, and the older combinatorial bounds of about (1/2)log n may be in PPP. Suggest adding this to the why.

M_fixed: Let $M=\{c\in\mathbb C:(f_c^{n}(0))_{n\ge0}\text{ bounded}\}$, $f_c(z)=z^2+c$. Prove or disprove that $M\cap\mathbb Q(i)$ is a decidable subset of $\mathbb Q(i)$. $\mathbb Q(i)\setminus M$ is r.e. For each $n$, the existence of an $n$-cycle with multiplier of modulus $\le1$ is decidable for algebraic $c$ (Tarski), and such a cycle forces $c\in M$. $M\cap\mathbb Z[i]$ is a finite, explicitly computable set (it contains the Misiurewicz points $-2,\pm i$, whose cycles are all repelling). So a positive answer would follow from (*): every $c\in(M\cap\mathbb Q(i))\setminus\mathbb Z[i]$ has a non-repelling cycle. Prove or disprove (*). (Example: $c=(37+16i)/100$ lies on the main cardioid with multiplier $(3+4i)/5$, a Siegel parameter.)
partial_result_check: The reduction is correct apart from one flaw. A non-repelling cycle implies c in M, since by Fatou all cycles are repelling when c is outside M. The example arithmetic checks out: mu/2-mu^2/4=(37+16i)/100. But (*) as stated is FALSE. c=-2 and c=+-i are Gaussian-integer Misiurewicz parameters in M with all cycles repelling (c=i: 0->i->-1+i->-i->-1+i). The fix excludes Z[i], where membership is a finite check.
notes: Not novel: Potgieter (arXiv cs/0604003, Sec. 2.3) asks exactly this and leaves it open. Found no later resolution. Stays A only because of its importance and the sharpened (*). Could fairly be downgraded on novelty.
